standard_prerequisites.name: The map A^h -> A^wedge induces a surjection from the minimal primes of A^wedge to the minimal primes of A^h, and branches(A) is at most branches(A^wedge)
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the comparison map between the two branch sets.

standard_prerequisites.name: Both branch sets are finite, the henselization and the completion being Noetherian
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the surjection into a bijectivity criterion.

core_obligations: The nr-branches-completion lemma gives a surjection from the set of branches of A^wedge onto the set of branches of A, together with the inequality of the counts (proof lines 31972-31973). Both sets are finite: the branches of a Noetherian ring are its finitely many minimal primes of the henselization respectively the completion, which are Noetherian by the henselization-noetherian lemma and the irreducible-components lemma of the algebra chapter (proof lines 31974-31977). A surjection between finite sets is a bijection exactly when the counts agree; by part (1) of the nr-branches-completion lemma the count agrees exactly when the radical of q A^wedge is prime for every minimal prime q of A^h, which is the stated equivalence (proof lines 31973-31977).
proof_roadmap: Set up the surjection between branch sets from the nr-branches-completion lemma (proof lines 31972-31973).
Use finiteness of both branch sets to convert count equality into the primeness criterion (proof lines 31974-31977).
